title: A small filtered category admits a final functor from a nonempty directed set
statement: Let $\mathcal J$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then there exist a nonempty directed set $(A,\le)$, regarded as a category with exactly one morphism $a\to b$ when $a\le b$ and none otherwise, and a functor $F:A\to\mathcal J$ which is final (cofinal in the sense of Stacks, Categories, Definition 04E6), that is: (1) for every object $y$ of $\mathcal J$ there exist $a\in A$ and a morphism $y\to F(a)$ in $\mathcal J$; (2) for every object $y$ of $\mathcal J$, all $a,a'\in A$ and all morphisms $b:y\to F(a)$, $b':y\to F(a')$ there exist a sequence $a=a_0\ge a_1\le a_2\ge a_3\le\cdots\le a_{2n}=a'$ in $A$ and morphisms $b_i:y\to F(a_i)$ ($0\le i\le 2n$) with $b_0=b$, $b_{2n}=b'$, $F(a_{2k+1}\to a_{2k})\circ b_{2k+1}=b_{2k}$ and $F(a_{2k+1}\to a_{2k+2})\circ b_{2k+1}=b_{2k+2}$ for $k=0,\ldots,n-1$.
